I took a walk along the new Chicago Riverwalk the other day, because the weather was so nice. For those who haven't been yet, here is a list of the restaurants down there, from east to west:

Island Party Hut: Of all the restaurants on the Riverwalk, this one feels the most like a laid-back neighborhood bar. It is east of Columbus drive in the grassy area under some trees. The bar itself is in a customized shipping container that has been wrapped to look like bamboo, and they serve a lot of rum drinks. It looks like they have pig roasts from time to time, and there's a bags board off to one side. You can sit by the water in the grass with your drink: this is the only one of the various Riverwalk restaurants where you can do that. Everyone else is on concrete or a patio of some sort. This would be a good place to go if you want to feel like you are at a neighborhood barbeque.

Cyrano's: This restaurant is a sprawling collection of structures to the east of where all the tour boat docks are. It's got a garden theme going. I didn't see many people there which is a good thing because I saw only one waiter for what looks like a large operation, but it is pretty enough.

O'Brien's: This is an outpost of O'Brien's Restaurant in Old Town, with a similar menu. This looks like the sort of place family place you could take your parents or your kids, though I could also imagine lunch with co-workers. Unlike Cyrano's they looked to be doing a brisk lunch business. The tables are farther back from the water, though raised above the main walkway. The look of the place reminds me of the patio room at the main O'Brien's.

City Winery: Really nice modern-looking set up in the new part of the Riverwalk. I can imagine this appealing to adults in their 20's and 30's without kids in tow. There are barstools where you can sit facing the river to watch the boats go by and/or the hourly rate marina that is right in front of it. Because of its position, it also gets a lot of nice sun around lunchtime. It was busy as heck.

Flanders' Beer & Fries: Also a nice looking, if minimalist, set up. All they have for food are really tasty French (Belgian) fries with different dips, and pretzels. Good beer selection, though not much of it local, wine, and soft drinks. Because they don't have a food menu, this is a good place for a first date. If it goes well, keep going down the Riverwalk on to a place with other food. If it doesn't , when the fries are gone, say goodbye. Also good for just meeting up with friends and hanging out, but with the limited menu you will eventually want to go somewhere else.

Has anyone else tried these? I've gone to Flanders and Island Party Hut so far--bookending my walk with booze. But I don't know how the food is at the other places.
